# Plinius research review and proposed agenda

9 October 2026

**Change the central research question to: which ink information survives acquisition and rendering, and how can a model learn to use it across specimens?** The current programme has established reliable computation and several useful negative results. It has not established a model with a material, retained improvement. Further small adjustments to the same adaptation recipe have a low expected information return.

My strongest research bet is **learning from paired observations of the same physical material at different acquisition qualities**, using the better observation as training information for a model that must operate on the poorer observation. First establish a small experiment that separates local learnability, transfer failure and information loss. Keep a second, conditional track for uncertain surface placement. This proposal changes the research direction; it does not claim these methods already work or are novel.

The governing objective is the [research charter](snapshot/research/lab/RESEARCH_CHARTER.md): defensible information recovery and leading methods, with prizes as an optional application. PHerc0800 need not remain the development target if another specimen provides a more informative scientific comparison.

## What the experiments establish

The research branch at commit `457a83b080714e2aeda86097809c9af73f8dfccc` contains 39 reports. All 36 reports in the restored cloud lab match their archived counterparts byte for byte; the branch supplies experiments 37–39. The [reconciliation](SOURCE_RECONCILIATION.json) records this check. The [experiment index](snapshot/research/EXPERIMENTS.md) provides the complete history.

| Evidence | Finding | Consequence for the new agenda |
|---|---|---|
| Experiments 1–5 | PHerc0800 responses persisted across larger contexts and source checks, without authenticated letters. | Stop following stronger detector responses with larger crops. Source correspondence alone cannot establish ink. |
| 6–7 and 22–24 | Dense supervision and native training help some references and hurt others. Uniform depth reversal worsens both Paris parent aggregates. | Treat acquisition and specimen dependence as variables to measure. The record does not support a universal checkpoint replacement or reversal correction. |
| 8–14 | A real first-step overshoot was identified. Lower learning rate stabilized training; recalibration recovered one domain but not Frag4. | Optimization bugs and score calibration explain part of the early record, not the remaining ranking failures. |
| 16–17 | Paris2 baseline AUROC ranges from 0.446 to 0.904. Optical labels align strongly with their registered infrared images; CT–optical registration residuals remain unmeasured. | Determine why nearby regions within a parent differ so much before assuming model capacity is the bottleneck. |
| 18, 20–21 | Explicit depth features and prediction preservation can beat matched controls while failing baseline retention. | Another small feature adapter is a weak next bet. These results do not exclude a model that explicitly represents uncertain geometry. |
| 25–36 | A historical interpolation defect was reproduced; fixed depth averaging failed; simple CT features and the texture-depth proxy did not establish physical ink depth. | Reuse the engineering. Stop generic provenance searches and intensity/depth sweeps on the same Frag6 regions. |
| 37 | Extending full-network training from 32 to 512 updates improves fit and gives a modest transfer gain. Adding Dice improves training further but worsens transfer. | “Train longer” and “restore Dice” have already received meaningful tests in this setup. Neither justifies continuing the same trajectory. |
| 38–39 | Broader supervision improves worst-region retention; a fixed prediction midpoint does not reproduce its aggregate/retention tradeoff. | Coverage is a useful lead. It remains confounded with reduced exposure to the original training source. |

The latest historical improvement criterion is **at least +0.01 absolute equal-parent Paris average precision (AP), with no regional AP or AUROC loss exceeding 0.02**. Some studies additionally require +0.01 over their matched control. These are practical development criteria, not significance tests. Older experiments used different screens; they should retain their original decisions.

| Latest comparison | Paris AP | AP gain over seed42 | Worst regional AP change | Worst regional AUROC change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Seed42 | 0.312384 | — | — | — |
| Narrow-source continuation, 512 updates | 0.317344 | +0.004960 | −0.025821 | −0.018205 |
| Broader coverage, 512 updates | 0.316197 | +0.003813 | −0.002464 | −0.002522 |
| Fixed 50/50 prediction midpoint | 0.315147 | +0.002762 | −0.009638 | −0.007936 |

These values were reproduced from the replay capsule, rather than transcribed only from a report. All 93 files verified; all 64 AP/AUROC values, eight scoring masks and reported decisions reproduced. See the [replay receipt](replay/REPLAY_RECEIPT.json), [numerical verification](replay/replay-result/VERIFICATION.json) and [comparison figure](latest-comparison.png). This replay verifies saved-map analysis, not the earlier neural training execution.

## Why progress has stalled

**The programme has explored a narrow training distribution.** Most continuations reuse two PHerc0139 regions. Experiment 38 increases unique supervised pixels from 54,701 to 110,014, adding one PHerc1667 crop, while halving PHerc0139 patch exposure. That is an informative controlled pilot, but it provides little coverage of specimen, ink, scan and geometry variation. Thirty-nine studies are not thirty-nine independent tests of broad generalization.

**Training fit has become a weak guide to the goal.** In experiment 37, the Dice arm's hard-label training BCE falls from 0.306468 at update 32 to 0.250895 at update 512, while Paris AP improves by only 0.000038. This is direct evidence against using further training-loss reduction as a reason to continue that recipe. It does not identify whether the limiting factor is annotation, acquisition, representation or geometry.

**The objective rewards staying near the old model.** An analytical observation helps interpret this. For one independently adjustable output probability, the current smoothed BCE plus unit-weight teacher KL has optimum `p* = (q + p_teacher)/2`, where `q` is 0.25 or 0.75. Both terms therefore constrain the new target. This is a useful stability mechanism, but supplies no new measurement of ink. The formula is a per-output idealization, not a description of the coupled network optimum, and it does not prove why AP fails. Experiment 37 already shows that adding a stronger fitting term is insufficient.

**The evaluation panel cannot resolve several competing causes.** Its large pixel counts come from very few physical parents, repeatedly consulted during development. Supplied labels have incomplete lineage; some optical registration is unresolved. PHerc0814's near-ceiling agreement is useful for retention, with limited headroom for discovery. Broad architectural conclusions would exceed this evidence.

My inference is that the next constraint to address is the combination of acquisition diversity and reference quality. Geometry and irrecoverable signal loss remain plausible alternatives. The record does not justify declaring either one the sole cause.

## What the literature changes

The June 2026 PHerc1667 paper describes a coupled acquisition, geometry, ink-recovery and expert-review pipeline. Its PHercParis4 case offers a particularly useful physical anchor: deposits visible in the high-resolution CT, alongside comparison with the older scan of the same material. That motivates paired acquisition experiments. It does not make every published model mask independent truth. [Angelotti et al., 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.29085v1)

The topography study distinguishes **a model trained at fine resolution failing on coarsened input** from **a model trained at the coarser resolution**. Those are different questions. Its heterogeneous cross-papyrus transfer and resolution effects support testing both here. Optical profilometry on opened fragments does not establish a universal CT resolution threshold or prove that PHerc0800 is unreadable. [Angelotti et al., Scientific Reports, 2026](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-58467-1)

The maintained Vesuvius pipeline already supports native 3D ink learning with a channel identifying the intended wrap. Its purpose is directly relevant to neighboring-sheet contamination. A small comparison against that representation would be more informative than calling another nominal-depth channel a new geometry method. [Official ink tutorial](https://scrollprize.org/tutorial5)

Two wider ML ideas are useful building blocks. Generalized distillation permits a teacher to use information unavailable to the deployed student. Multiple-instance learning provides a way to supervise a collection of candidate locations without knowing which location contains the signal. Neither is a new invention of this programme. [Lopez-Paz et al., 2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03643); [Ilse et al., 2018](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/ilse18a.html)

Model selection itself is part of a domain-generalization method. Strong conventional training deserves a fair baseline before attributing gains to special adaptation machinery. [Gulrajani and Lopez-Paz, 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.01434)

## The first study should identify the bottleneck

**Question:** can a fixed learner recover reference-supported ink on new regions from the same acquisition, and what happens when that observation is degraded or replaced by a real coarse scan?

Start with a small positive-control panel on PHercParis4, where modern CT permits checking deposits directly, plus a second development parent with a documented reference. Select regions using geometry, reference coverage and acquisition properties before candidate predictions. Include convincing ink, verified background, difficult structure and ambiguous material. Ambiguous material remains unknown. The first deliverable is a table linking each region to its physical coordinates, usable reference and admissible claim; it need not be an elaborate new provenance framework.

Keep the old Paris panel as a regression panel. A within-parent training arm must use different physical regions and exclude overlapping input context. Do not train on an old evaluation region and continue to call it held out. Begin with three fixed conditions:

1. **Native observation, training and evaluation within one acquisition domain.** Compare a suitable frozen baseline with an ordinary supervised learner fitted on the separate training regions. Include a tiny training-fit check to distinguish an implementation failure from poor transfer.
2. **Synthetically degraded observation of the same material.** Apply one prespecified physical sampling/blur/noise recipe in volume coordinates and retrain at that observation quality. Also evaluate the native-trained model on degraded inputs as a separate mismatch control. Preserve the physical field of view and label support.
3. **A real coarse acquisition of the same material**, conditional on validated registration. Use structural landmarks excluded from fitting to measure alignment uncertainty. Match the scored physical support. Degraded fine CT is not a substitute for this arm: energy, phase retrieval, scattering and noise differ.

The comparison must include a suitable contemporary baseline for each input contract. Seed42 remains the approximately 9 µm reference; the canonical approximately 2 µm ResNet-152 is a separate family from the paper's ResNet3D-50 ablation. Do not interpolate a coarse tensor and call it a native-resolution baseline. [Official canonical model card](https://huggingface.co/scrollprize/ink_canonical_2um)

| Outcome | Research decision |
|---|---|
| Within-domain learning improves disjoint regions; transfer fails | Prioritize acquisition/specimen transfer and broader supervision. |
| Native learning works; matched retraining on degraded data fails | Investigate which signal the degradation removes. This is evidence conditional on the degradation and tested learner, not an impossibility theorem. |
| Synthetic coarse data works; registered real coarse data fails | Prioritize real acquisition differences; more pooled fine data alone is unlikely to close the gap. |
| Only geometry-corrected views work | Advance the uncertain-geometry track below. |
| Training fit works but disjoint native regions remain weak | Revisit reference reliability and local biological variation before increasing model size. |
| Even the training-fit check fails | Fix the data/model contract before interpreting scientific failure. |

Score paired AP changes, AUROC, sensitivity at a development-fixed operating point, and retained coverage. Report every physical region. For promotion retain the historical +0.01 AP and −0.02 retention criteria, applied to a prospectively specified panel and its appropriate baseline. For this diagnostic, the pattern across conditions is the main result. A tiny pilot has descriptive uncertainty; pixels cannot provide independent replication.

Time-box reference admission to one bounded acquisition/annotation exercise. If a real paired scan cannot be registered, deliver the native-versus-synthetic comparison with that limitation and move to another documented pair. Avoid another succession of metadata-only phases on an unchanged missing source.

## The main research bet is privileged acquisition training

**Hypothesis:** a better observation of the same material can teach a coarse-input model which surviving features matter more effectively than preserving the coarse model's own predictions.

On development material with usable pairing, use native fine CT and reviewed volumetric deposits—or reliably registered optical evidence—as training-only information. The student receives only the intended coarse CT input. Compare three students with identical architecture, training regions and update exposure: ordinary supervised learning; supervision plus a coarse-input teacher control; and supervision plus a fine-observation teacher. Keep the amount of trusted supervision constant. Give uncertain teacher targets an explicit mask or weight fixed on training/development material.

The contribution would be the physical pairing, treatment of uncertainty and demonstrated transfer, rather than distillation itself. The key control asks whether a privileged teacher helps because it sees additional evidence, rather than because another loss term or more labels were added. Reserve complete physical regions and eventually a separate parent before selecting the method. Teacher predictions on a test region cannot also define its ground truth.

Do not optimize a photorealistic or letter-looking super-resolution image. Optimize recovery against independent image-supported evidence. A student cannot reconstruct information absent from its input merely because the teacher sees it. Include texture-matched background, ambiguous regions and a spatially mispaired-teacher control; an apparent improvement that survives arbitrary teacher mispairing would challenge the claimed mechanism.

**Advance** only with a repeated AP gain over the supervised and coarse-teacher controls, preserved false-positive behavior and coverage, and improvement on another physical region. **Stop** this route if benefits occur only on synthetic degradation, teacher-derived test masks, or a single training parent. Treat such outcomes as boundaries of the method, not reasons for a larger unqualified run.

## A conditional track should marginalize uncertain geometry

**Hypothesis:** premature commitment to one sampled surface or depth window discards useful evidence or admits neighboring-wrap signal.

Represent a small, physically constrained set of plausible surface positions and normals. Predict ink while integrating over these alternatives, and retain an unguided full-depth path. Add wrap identity when known. Missing, ambiguous and censored positions require separate states; the texture-transition proxy from experiment 36 must not become an anatomical label.

The original baseline already learns depth fusion, and equal averaging was tested in experiment 32. A meaningful comparison therefore needs the fixed baseline, uniform multi-view averaging, a capacity-matched learned aggregator without geometry, and the geometry-conditioned version. An attention weight is not a verified ink depth. Supervise or check localization separately wherever actual 3D deposits provide evidence.

First use counterfactual controls with the signal held fixed: shift the proposed surface, insert a misleading stronger texture interface, place ink beyond the candidate search range, and place deposits on a neighboring wrap. Measure missed ink, wrong-wrap attribution, false certainty and coverage. These controls test the mechanism. Real evaluation must then show a benefit in regions with independently measured placement uncertainty, rather than only in invented perturbations.

Advance if the method outperforms uniform averaging and the matched unguided model while handling wrong-wrap and out-of-range cases. If the benefit vanishes with corrected geometry, prefer correcting the rendering. This is a conditional second track, not the next automatic continuation of Frag6.

## A cheap bridge can settle the coverage confound

Experiment 39's proposed second PHerc1667 crop is a reasonable replication, but it cannot by itself distinguish added diversity from reduced PHerc0139 exposure. Replace that default next step with one fixed exposure experiment when a runnable training bundle is available:

- **A:** the original two PHerc0139 patches per update.
- **B:** keep one PHerc0139 patch; set the removed slot's supervised and preservation losses to zero while retaining the same per-slot weighting. This tests reduced source exposure.
- **C:** use exactly B's retained PHerc0139 slot plus the matched PHerc1667 replacement. This is the mixed-source condition.

Use one fixed objective and update budget, identical retained-slot schedules, and report source-specific loss and gradient contribution. C versus B necessarily adds learning signal; this design estimates the value of adding that source relative to removing the original exposure, not a metaphysically pure effect of “diversity.” Avoid renormalizing B into a full-weight single-source update. A fixed gradient-alignment diagnostic on training-only sources could motivate later work, but should not be used to select a winning recipe on the old test panel.

This is a bounded supporting study. It should not delay the paired-acquisition panel. Further source-region replication becomes worthwhile if C has a repeatable benefit beyond B. Keep the original phase38 and phase39 failures unchanged.

## Execution order and decision discipline

The next work package should deliver the learnability/degradation panel and one conventional baseline comparison. Use the outcome to select either privileged-acquisition training or geometry marginalization. Run the small exposure control alongside panel preparation only if its inputs are already available. Promote one candidate to a new physical-parent evaluation after development choices are fixed.

Preserve the old eight-region regression panel and leave PHerc0009B, PHerc0500P2 and PHerc0841 untouched until a specific evaluation role is assigned. Their incomplete ancestry does not prohibit all research; it limits which claims they can support. Distinguish supplied-reference agreement, new-supervision generalization and authenticated ink recovery explicitly. A cleanly initialized model may make some exposure questions easier, at a greater training cost.
